topic-064-psi-sampler-initial-particle-s.evolution: Earlier representatives frame data generation as sequential decision-making. Later work develops diffusion planners, shortcut sampling, and infeasibility detection. Recent methods optimize latent priors, analyze likelihood estimation in reinforcement learning, and learn variable-length insertion orders, widening the forms of structured generation available for planning and combinatorial tasks.
openQuestions: How can a planner certify feasibility while sampling from a learned generative prior?
When is learning a better proposal more effective than correcting samples afterward?
topic-064-psi-sampler-initial-particle-s.overview: Generative models can represent distributions over trajectories or structured solutions rather than choose one action at a time. This topic studies how diffusion and related sequence models are guided toward high-value, feasible behavior. Learning the starting distribution, modifying sampling, and choosing a generation order are alternative ways to influence the final plan.
topic-064-psi-sampler-initial-particle-s.title: Generative Policies and Diffusion-Based Planning
topic-064-psi-sampler-initial-particle-s.whyItMatters: A plausible trajectory is not necessarily executable or rewarding. Guidance must improve decisions without causing distribution drift or making inference so expensive that the planner loses its practical advantage.

topic-065-a-closer-look-at-smoothness-in.evolution: Early representatives explore adversarial feature transformations and controlled invariance. Later work develops scalable certification and explicit accuracy–robustness tradeoffs. Recent applications extend to imaging and text scoring, while analyses of CLIP defenses show why apparent test-time robustness can disappear when the attack targets the defense’s own decision rule.
openQuestions: Which certified threat models correspond to meaningful real-world perturbations?
How can evaluation detect a defense that merely changes which attacks are effective?
topic-065-a-closer-look-at-smoothness-in.overview: Adversarial robustness concerns predictions under deliberately chosen input changes. These papers study certified noise-based defenses, robust training, feature sensitivity, minimal perturbations, and test-time protection. A central distinction is between measured resistance to a fixed attack and a guarantee that holds across the perturbations allowed by the threat model.
topic-065-a-closer-look-at-smoothness-in.title: Adversarial Robustness and Adaptive Defense Evaluation
topic-065-a-closer-look-at-smoothness-in.whyItMatters: Defenses can rely on assumptions about how adversarial examples differ from clean inputs. An adaptive evaluator may exploit those assumptions, so robustness claims need both suitable attacks and clear definitions of the permitted changes.

topic-066-f-trajectory-balance-a-loss-fa.evolution: Earlier representatives include probability-flow learning and continuous-time density models. Recent flow-matching work uses minibatch couplings, energy formulations, and learned forward processes. The newest examples add history and spatial context to shortcut flows, while other studies examine transport variants and membership signals along interpolation paths.
openQuestions: Which path properties predict low-step sample quality before full training?
How can efficient transport retain diversity without exposing additional memorization signals?
topic-066-f-trajectory-balance-a-loss-fa.overview: Flow-based generators learn how to move a simple distribution toward data through a continuous vector field. This topic studies the choice of paths, couplings, conditioning, and objectives that make that transport easier to learn and sample. Straighter or less ambiguous trajectories can reduce the number of evaluations needed for generation.
topic-066-f-trajectory-balance-a-loss-fa.title: Flow Matching and Efficient Probability Transport
topic-066-f-trajectory-balance-a-loss-fa.whyItMatters: A mathematically valid path can still be inefficient numerically. Choosing how noise and examples are paired affects gradient variance, transport cost, and the speed–quality tradeoff of the resulting sampler.

topic-067-a-bayesian-method-for-reducing.evolution: Early representatives study cell assemblies, receptive fields, and Bayesian signal classification. Later work adds integrate-and-fire estimation and low-dimensional count dynamics. Recent examples fit summary statistics through stochastic simulation and pursue large-scale biophysical models, while some adjacent work transfers spiking mechanisms into robust sensory processing.
openQuestions: Which summary statistics distinguish realistic circuits from merely good predictive fits?
How can uncertainty about unobserved neurons be carried into connectivity or stimulation conclusions?
topic-067-a-bayesian-method-for-reducing.overview: Neural recordings contain discrete spikes, variable counts, and partially observed population dynamics. This cluster develops probabilistic spike models, latent dynamical systems, and differentiable simulators to connect those observations with circuit behavior. It examines which statistics a fitted model must reproduce to be a credible account of the recorded activity.
topic-067-a-bayesian-method-for-reducing.title: Statistical Models of Neural Spiking and Population Activity
topic-067-a-bayesian-method-for-reducing.whyItMatters: High likelihood alone may not yield realistic simulated neural behavior. Hidden neurons and mismatched variability can distort inferred connectivity, so models need checks on population statistics and dynamics as well as prediction fit.

topic-068-a-bayesian-framework-to-integr.evolution: Early representatives connect Bayesian model comparison and neural representations. Later work scales network learning through treewidth constraints and compact conditional tables. Recent methods place differentiable latent distributions over graphs and develop probabilistic routing on constrained domains, combining flexible structure with sparse computations and explicit uncertainty.
openQuestions: How can graph-posterior approximations preserve competing causal explanations?
When does enforcing tractable structure introduce more error than the resulting computational savings justify?
topic-068-a-bayesian-framework-to-integr.overview: Bayesian structure learning infers relationships among variables while retaining uncertainty about the graph itself. These papers study bounded-treewidth networks, low-rank conditional models, incomplete temporal data, and differentiable graph distributions. Related hierarchical and tree-based models exploit structure to make posterior computation and interpretation manageable.
topic-068-a-bayesian-framework-to-integr.title: Bayesian Graph Structure and Hierarchical Models
topic-068-a-bayesian-framework-to-integr.whyItMatters: Selecting one graph can conceal multiple explanations compatible with limited observations. Posterior structure matters for interventions and subsequent inference, while computational constraints determine which dependencies can realistically be represented.

topic-069-pscaling-small-models-principl.evolution: Early examples develop stochastic descent and weight-specific training schemes. Later work tackles meta-training pathologies and scalable learned optimizers. Recent analyses examine large-model variance reduction, optimizer-specific implicit bias, and zeroth-order stability governed by broader Hessian-spectrum information than in ordinary first-order updates.
openQuestions: Which learned update rules transfer beyond the tasks used to train the optimizer?
Can practical diagnostics anticipate instability without computing a full curvature spectrum?
topic-069-pscaling-small-models-principl.overview: Optimizers determine both how quickly a network learns and which solution it reaches. This cluster studies learned update rules, lookahead, variance reduction, curvature methods, warmup, and gradient-free dynamics. The representatives examine optimization as a dynamical process whose stability and implicit bias can matter as much as short-term loss reduction.
topic-069-pscaling-small-models-principl.title: Optimizer Design, Learned Updates, and Stability
topic-069-pscaling-small-models-principl.whyItMatters: A faster training-loss decrease need not improve generalization, and learned optimizers can fail because their own training gradients are biased or unstable. Wall-clock cost, validation behavior, and stability boundaries provide complementary measures of progress.

topic-070-a-new-framework-for-cybersecur.evolution: The cluster begins in 2024 with extensible agent environments, control protocols, and reward-hacking studies. Subsequent work adds realistic vulnerability benchmarks and indirect-injection defenses. Recent representatives examine activation monitoring, unsafe computer use, and failures of embedding-based message screening, emphasizing that malicious and benign text can look similar in representation space.
openQuestions: How can agents maintain useful tool access while enforcing clear trust boundaries?
Which monitoring signals remain reliable after several rounds of adversarial communication?
topic-070-a-new-framework-for-cybersecur.overview: Tool-using agents encounter untrusted documents, external services, and messages from other agents. This topic evaluates prompt injection, malicious tool selection, unintended actions, and deliberate subversion within those workflows. Defenses include monitoring, communication filtering, and designs that preserve boundaries between task instructions and external data.
topic-070-a-new-framework-for-cybersecur.title: Security and Control of Tool-Using Agent Systems
topic-070-a-new-framework-for-cybersecur.whyItMatters: Safety of individual text responses does not ensure safety of executed actions. Evaluation must test the system’s authority, information flow, and feedback loops, including ordinary-task failures that occur even without an attacker.

topic-071-mathttvits-variational-inferen.evolution: Early representatives develop Gaussian-process, linear, and generalized-linear bandits. Later work sharpens exploration and posterior-sampling guarantees across structured settings. Recent analyses study variance-aware policies, safety–inference tradeoffs, and an optimization interpretation of Thompson sampling in which residual uncertainty regularizes greedy behavior.
openQuestions: How can posterior-sampling methods remain reliable when their model is misspecified?
What tradeoff is unavoidable between low regret and accurate statistical inference about rarely chosen actions?
topic-071-mathttvits-variational-inferen.overview: Bandit algorithms choose actions while learning their rewards, balancing immediate value against information that improves later choices. This cluster studies structured and contextual models, Thompson sampling, implicit exploration, and high-probability regret. It asks how much exploration is necessary and how uncertainty should influence action selection.
topic-071-mathttvits-variational-inferen.title: Bandit Regret and Uncertainty-Driven Exploration
topic-071-mathttvits-variational-inferen.whyItMatters: Forcing uniform exploration can waste effort on poor actions, but insufficient exploration can lock a learner into a mistake. Strong guarantees help distinguish efficient uncertainty management from lucky performance on a particular reward sequence.
